key_insight: CuAD generates tangent and adjoint CUDA kernels directly from source, enabling accurate GPU-based sensitivities without storing an intermediate-value tape.
engineering_relevance: GPU-native discrete adjoints can support aerodynamic optimization, inverse design and flow-data assimilation while avoiding finite-difference sensitivity errors.
method: Transform CUDA kernels into ordinary CUDA tangent and adjoint source.
Organize reverse mode around GPU threads, recomputing intermediates instead of storing a tape.
Use atomic adjoint updates only where multiple threads access the same memory.
evidence_signal: Across four flow-model kernels, derivatives agreed with finite differences and passed adjoint dot-product tests to round-off; adjoints cost 2–6× primal execution, and CuAD was 16–470× faster than Clad on the summation kernel.
watch_item: Evaluation covers simple flow-model kernels; scalability and compatibility with full production CFD solvers remain to be demonstrated.
paper_title: CuAD: Source-to-Source Automatic Differentiation of CUDA Kernels for Discrete Adjoints in Computational Fluid Dynamics
